evidence: 2026-09-30: real signup through the Agent Vault proxy using this recipe (MCP session, vault-minted password); all three selectors matched. After Sign up came a birthday step (month, day and year dropdowns, then Next) and a blog-name step; the page then went on to onboarding and Tumblr's "Verify your email address" mail arrived at the signup address. The account owner opened its link, which showed a CAPTCHA and then a button to verify the email, and completed both. A fresh sign-in with the same credentials was then accepted.
gotchas: Claims www.tumblr.com only: every tumblr.com subdomain is a user's blog, not Tumblr's own signup.

After Sign up come a birthday step (three <select> dropdowns for month, day and year; Next stays disabled until all three are set) and a blog-name step (the blog's public name, not a sign-in name; sign-in is by email).
The header's Search box is a visible text input on every step; target the signup fields by name, not by type=text.
The emailed verification link opens a page with a CAPTCHA and then a button to verify the email; both are the account owner's.

2026-10-09: the birthday selects are select[name="month"], select[name="day"], select[name="year"] (pick by value, e.g. month 3); the blog-name box is input[name="blogName"] and the final button is 'Sign up' again.

After signing in from a European egress, a consent iframe covers the page (buttons 'Agree' / 'OK' inside the frame); a click into it timed out through the proxy and detect_challenge does not classify it.
